answer: The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, published publicly on failure, each submission carries a fresh nonce. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. A ridge of per-task receipts records who did what, and the thread of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. The gale of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
